newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: STOCKS WEEK - INDEX RISES IN LOWER VOLUMES.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS WEEK - INDEX RISES IN LOWER VOLUMES.

text.p: Shares on the Botswana Stock
Exchange continued to rise last week amid smaller volumes.
The domestic index added 12.01 points to close at 471.87.
There was strong foreign interest in brewery holding company
Sechaba , pushing the stock up 25 thebe to 375 thebe.
Gains were also seen in Barclays , up five thebe to
755 thebe, Botswana Insurance also up five thebe to 250
thebe, First National up 10 thebe to 520 thebe and
milling company and food wholesaler Sefalana up 10
thebe to 455 thebe.
Trading unchanged were security group Inco at 90
thebe, investment company Kgolo ya Sechaba 190 thebe and
Standard Chartered 630 thebe.
Engen fell five thebe on the week.
Untraded were food and tobacco wholesaler Metsef ,
clothing chain Pep and variable loan stock counter RDC
Properties .
Domestic turnover was down to 204,424 shares from 563,475,
for value 725,856 pula against 1,701,510 pula.
On the foreign board, De Beers was the only counter
to trade. It traded 320 shares at the unchanged price of 12,791
thebe.
Untraded and unchanged were Regent Undervalued Assets
Fund at 4,000 thebe and McCarthy Retail group
at 1,100 thebe.
The foreign index lost 0.64 points to close at 391.21
points. The all companies index also dropped, shedding 0.32
points to 393.27.
